### 3.4 `src/models.rs` — **FIX**: Removido `&` no `e.to_string()`

```rust
// crates/arkhe-local-llm-manager/src/models.rs
use std::fs;
use std::path::Path;
use thiserror::Error;

#[derive(Error, Debug)]
pub enum ModelError {
    #[error("Model file not found at {0}")]
    NotFound(String),
    #[error("FS Error: {0}")]
    FsError(#[from] std::io::Error),
    #[error("Ollama API Error: {0}")]
    OllamaError(String),
}

pub struct ModelManager;

impl ModelManager {
    /// Remove um modelo GGUF/Safetensors do disco.
    pub fn remove_local_model(path: &str) -> Result<(), ModelError> {
        let p = Path::new(path);
        if !p.exists() {
            return Err(ModelError::NotFound(path.to_string()));
        }

        if p.is_dir() {
            fs::remove_dir_all(p)?;
        } else {
            fs::remove_file(p)?;
        }

        tracing::info!("🗑️ Local model removed: {}", path);
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Remove um modelo Ollama via API (POST /api/delete com JSON body).
    pub async fn remove_ollama_model(model_name: &str) -> Result<(), ModelError> {
        let url = "http://localhost:11434/api/delete";

        // Client sem proxy para localhost
        let client = reqwest::Client::builder()
            .no_proxy()
            .build()
            .map_err(|e| ModelError::FsError(std::io::Error::new(
                std::io::ErrorKind::Other,
                // ✅ FIX: String owned, não referência
                e.to_string(),
            )))?;

        let body = serde_json::json!({"name": model_name});

        let res = client
            .post(url)
            .json(&body)
            .send()
            .await
            .map_err(|e| {
                // ✅ FIX: String owned, não referência
                ModelError::OllamaError(e.to_string())
            })?;

        if res.status().is_success() {
            tracing::info!("🗑️ Ollama model removed via API: {}", model_name);
            Ok(())
        } else {
            let status = res.status().as_u16();
            let text = res.text().await.unwrap_or_default();
            Err(ModelError::OllamaError(format!(
                "Ollama delete failed ({}): {}",
                status, text
            )))
        }
    }

    /// Lista modelos Ollama disponíveis.
    pub async fn list_ollama_models() -> Result<Vec<String>, ModelError> {
        let url = "http://localhost:11434/api/tags";

        let client = reqwest::Client::builder()
            .no_proxy()
            .build()
            .map_err(|e| ModelError::FsError(std::io::Error::new(
                std::io::ErrorKind::Other,
                e.to_string(),
            )))?;

        let res = client
            .get(url)
            .send()
            .await
            .map_err(|e| ModelError::OllamaError(e.to_string()))?;

        if !res.status().is_success() {
            return Err(ModelError::OllamaError(format!(
                "Ollama list failed: {}",
                res.status()
            )));
        }

        let json: serde_json::Value = res
            .json()
            .await
            .map_err(|e| ModelError::OllamaError(e.to_string()))?;

        let models = json
            .get("models")
            .and_then(|m| m.as_array())
            .map(|arr| {
                arr.iter()
                    .filter_map(|m| m.get("name")?.as_str().map(String::from))
                    .collect()
            })
            .unwrap_or_default();

        Ok(models)
    }

    /// Calcula o tamanho total de um diretório de modelo no disco.
    pub fn model_size_on_disk(path: &str) -> Result<u64, ModelError> {
        let p = Path::new(path);
        if !p.exists() {
            return Err(ModelError::NotFound(path.to_string()));
        }

        let mut total = 0u64;
        if p.is_dir() {
            for entry in fs::read_dir(p)? {
                let entry = entry?;
                let metadata = entry.metadata()?;
                if metadata.is_file() {
                    total += metadata.len();
                } else if metadata.is_dir() {
                    total += Self::model_size_on_disk(
                        entry.path().to_str().unwrap_or(""),
                    )?;
                }
            }
        } else {
            total = fs::metadata(p)?.len();
        }

        Ok(total)
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use tempfile::TempDir;

    #[test]
    fn test_remove_local_model_file() {
        let dir = TempDir::new().unwrap();
        let file_path = dir.path().join("model.gguf");
        fs::write(&file_path, b"fake model data").unwrap();

        assert!(file_path.exists());
        ModelManager::remove_local_model(file_path.to_str().unwrap()).unwrap();
        assert!(!file_path.exists());
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_remove_local_model_dir() {
        let dir = TempDir::new().unwrap();
        let sub_dir = dir.path().join("model_dir");
        fs::create_dir_all(sub_dir.join("shards")).unwrap();
        fs::write(sub_dir.join("config.json"), b"{}").unwrap();
        fs::write(sub_dir.join("shards/shard-01.gguf"), b"data").unwrap();

        assert!(sub_dir.exists());
        ModelManager::remove_local_model(sub_dir.to_str().unwrap()).unwrap();
        assert!(!sub_dir.exists());
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_remove_nonexistent_model() {
        let result = ModelManager::remove_local_model("/tmp/nonexistent_model_xyz.gguf");
        assert!(matches!(result, Err(ModelError::NotFound(_))));
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_model_size() {
        let dir = TempDir::new().unwrap();
        let file_path = dir.path().join("model.gguf");
        fs::write(&file_path, vec![0u8; 1024 * 1024]).unwrap(); // 1 MB

        let size = ModelManager::model_size_on_disk(file_path.to_str().unwrap()).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(size, 1024 * 1024);
    }
}
```

### 3.5 `src/systemd.rs` — **REESCRITO**: `zbus::Proxy` genérico com interface correta

```rust
// crates/arkhe-local-llm-manager/src/systemd.rs
//! Gerenciamento de serviços systemd via D-Bus.
//! Usa zbus::Proxy genérico — sem dependência de zbus-systemd.

use thiserror::Error;
use zbus::{Connection, Proxy};

#[derive(Error, Debug)]
pub enum SystemdError {
    #[error("D-Bus Connection Error: {0}")]
    DbusError(#[from] zbus::Error),
    #[error("Systemd unit {unit} failed to {action}: {reason}")]
    UnitFailed {
        unit: String,
        action: String,
        reason: String,
    },
}

/// Wrapper em torno do Proxy genérico do systemd1.Manager.
pub struct SystemdManager {
    proxy: Proxy<'static>,
}

impl SystemdManager {
    /// Conecta ao bus de sistema e cria o proxy do systemd.
    pub async fn new() -> Result<Self, SystemdError> {
        let connection = Connection::system().await?;

        // ✅ FIX: Proxy genérico com a interface correta do systemd
        let proxy = Proxy::new(
            connection,
            "org.freedesktop.systemd1",
            "/org/freedesktop/systemd1",
            "org.freedesktop.systemd1.Manager",
        )
        .await?;

        Ok(Self { proxy })
    }

    /// Normaliza o nome da unidade, adicionando ".service" se necessário.
    fn normalize_unit(name: &str) -> String {
        if name.contains('.') {
            name.to_string()
        } else {
            format!("{}.service", name)
        }
    }

    /// Para um serviço systemd de forma assíncrona via D-Bus.
    pub async fn stop_service(&self, unit_name: &str) -> Result<(), SystemdError> {
        let unit = Self::normalize_unit(unit_name);

        // StopUnit(unit_name, mode) retorna um object path para o job
        let result: Result<zbus::zvariant::OwnedObjectPath, zbus::Error> = self
            .proxy
            .call_method("StopUnit", &(unit.as_str(), "replace"))
            .await
            .and_then(|r| r.body().deserialize());

        match result {
            Ok(_job_path) => {
                tracing::info!("🛑 Systemd service stopped: {}", unit);
                Ok(())
            }
            Err(e) => {
                let err_str = e.to_string();
                // Ignorar se o serviço não existe ou já está parado
                if err_str.contains("org.freedesktop.systemd1.UnitNotFound")
                    || err_str.contains("org.freedesktop.DBus.Error.UnknownObject")
                {
                    tracing::warn!(
                        "Service {} not found or already stopped, continuing.",
                        unit
                    );
                    Ok(())
                } else {
                    Err(SystemdError::UnitFailed {
                        unit,
                        action: "stop".to_string(),
                        reason: err_str,
                    })
                }
            }
        }
    }

    /// Inicia um serviço systemd.
    pub async fn start_service(&self, unit_name: &str) -> Result<(), SystemdError> {
        let unit = Self::normalize_unit(unit_name);

        let result: Result<zbus::zvariant::OwnedObjectPath, zbus::Error> = self
            .proxy
            .call_method("StartUnit", &(unit.as_str(), "replace"))
            .await
            .and_then(|r| r.body().deserialize());

        match result {
            Ok(_job_path) => {
                tracing::info!("▶️ Systemd service started: {}", unit);
                Ok(())
            }
            Err(e) => Err(SystemdError::UnitFailed {
                unit,
                action: "start".to_string(),
                reason: e.to_string(),
            }),
        }
    }

    /// Reinicia um serviço systemd.
    pub async fn restart_service(&self, unit_name: &str) -> Result<(), SystemdError> {
        let unit = Self::normalize_unit(unit_name);

        let result: Result<zbus::zvariant::OwnedObjectPath, zbus::Error> = self
            .proxy
            .call_method("RestartUnit", &(unit.as_str(), "replace"))
            .await
            .and_then(|r| r.body().deserialize());

        match result {
            Ok(_job_path) => {
                tracing::info!("🔄 Systemd service restarted: {}", unit);
                Ok(())
            }
            Err(e) => Err(SystemdError::UnitFailed {
                unit,
                action: "restart".to_string(),
                reason: e.to_string(),
            }),
        }
    }

    /// Verifica o estado ativo de uma unidade.
    pub async fn is_active(&self, unit_name: &str) -> Result<bool, SystemdError> {
        let unit = Self::normalize_unit(unit_name);
        let unit_path = format!(
            "/org/freedesktop/systemd1/unit/{}",
            unit.replace('.', "_2e")
        );

        let unit_proxy = Proxy::new(
            self.proxy.connection().clone(),
            "org.freedesktop.systemd1",
            unit_path,
            "org.freedesktop.systemd1.Unit",
        )
        .await?;

        let active_state: Result<String, zbus::Error> = unit_proxy
            .get_property("ActiveState")
            .await
            .and_then(|p| p.get().await);

        match active_state {
            Ok(state) => Ok(state == "active"),
            Err(_) => Ok(false),
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn test_normalize_unit() {
        assert_eq!(
            SystemdManager::normalize_unit("nginx"),
            "nginx.service"
        );
        assert_eq!(
            SystemdManager::normalize_unit("nginx.service"),
            "nginx.service"
        );
        assert_eq!(
            SystemdManager::normalize_unit("docker.socket"),
            "docker.socket"
        );
    }
}
```

### 3.6 `src/lib.rs` — Orquestrador unificado (sem mudanças estruturais)

```rust
// crates/arkhe-local-llm-manager/src/lib.rs
pub mod docker;
pub mod models;
pub mod process;
pub mod systemd;

use thiserror::Error;

#[derive(Error, Debug)]
pub enum LlmManagerError {
    #[error("Process Error: {0}")]
    Process(#[from] process::ProcessError),
    #[error("Docker Error: {0}")]
    Docker(#[from] docker::DockerError),
    #[error("Model Error: {0}")]
    Model(#[from] models::ModelError),
    #[error("Systemd Error: {0}")]
    Systemd(#[from] systemd::SystemdError),
}

/// Métodos de desligamento suportados pelo orquestrador.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum ShutdownMethod {
    /// Mata um processo nativo por PID (SIGTERM → SIGKILL).
    Process,
    /// Para e remove um container Docker.
    Docker,
    /// Para um serviço systemd via D-Bus.
    Systemd,
    /// Remove um modelo do Ollama via API.
    OllamaModel,
    /// Remove arquivos de modelo do disco.
    File,
}

impl ShutdownMethod {
    pub fn from_str(s: &str) -> Option<Self> {
        match s {
            "process" => Some(Self::Process),
            "docker" => Some(Self::Docker),
            "systemd" => Some(Self::Systemd),
            "ollama_model" => Some(Self::OllamaModel),
            "file" => Some(Self::File),
            _ => None,
        }
    }
}

pub struct LocalLlmOrchestrator;

impl LocalLlmOrchestrator {
    /// Orquestra o desligamento completo de um ambiente de IA local.
    pub async fn shutdown(
        method: ShutdownMethod,
        target: &str,
    ) -> Result<(), LlmManagerError> {
        match method {
            ShutdownMethod::Process => {
                let pid: u32 = target
                    .parse()
                    .map_err(|_| process::ProcessError::NotFound(target.to_string()))?;
                tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || {
                    process::ProcessManager::stop_process_gracefully(pid.into(), 10)
                })
                .await??;
            }
            ShutdownMethod::Docker => {
                let docker = docker::DockerManager::new();
                docker.stop_and_remove_container(target).await?;
            }
            ShutdownMethod::Systemd => {
                let systemd = systemd::SystemdManager::new().await?;
                systemd.stop_service(target).await?;
            }
            ShutdownMethod::OllamaModel => {
                models::ModelManager::remove_ollama_model(target).await?;
            }
            ShutdownMethod::File => {
                models::ModelManager::remove_local_model(target)?;
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Desligamento completo: tenta todos os métodos aplicáveis para um alvo.
    pub async fn full_cleanup(target_name: &str) -> Result<Vec<String>, LlmManagerError> {
        let mut actions = Vec::new();

        // 1. Tentar parar processo nativo
        if let Ok(pid) = process::ProcessManager::find_pid_by_name(target_name) {
            let pid_u32: u32 = pid.into();
            tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || {
                process::ProcessManager::stop_process_gracefully(pid.into(), 10)
            })
            .await??;
            actions.push(format!("Killed process PID {}", pid_u32));
        }

        // 2. Tentar parar containers Docker
        let docker = docker::DockerManager::new();
        if docker.is_available().await {
            match docker.stop_and_remove_all_by_image(target_name).await {
                Ok(removed) => {
                    if !removed.is_empty() {
                        actions.push(format!("Removed {} Docker containers", removed.len()));
                    }
                }
                Err(e) => tracing::warn!("Docker cleanup failed: {}", e),
            }
        }

        // 3. Tentar parar serviço systemd
        match systemd::SystemdManager::new().await {
            Ok(sysd) => {
                if sysd.stop_service(target_name).await.is_ok() {
                    actions.push(format!("Stopped systemd service {}", target_name));
                }
            }
            Err(e) => tracing::warn!("Systemd unavailable: {}", e),
        }

        Ok(actions)
    }
}
```

```rust
// crates/arkhe-wormgraph/src/rdf.rs
//! RDF triplestore com SPARQL query engine conectado.
//!
//! Conforme W3C RDF 1.1 Concepts: https://www.w3.org/TR/rdf11-concepts/
//! Conforme W3C SPARQL 1.1 Query: https://www.w3.org/TR/sparql11-query/

use sophia::api::ns::Namespace;
use sophia::api::term::Term;
use sophia::inmem::graph::FastGraph;
use std::collections::BTreeMap;
use std::sync::LazyLock;
use thiserror::Error;

/// Namespaces padrão W3C — usando LazyLock (estável desde Rust 1.80).
pub mod ns {
    use super::Namespace;

    pub static RDF: LazyLock<Namespace> =
        LazyLock::new(|| Namespace::new("http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#").unwrap());
    pub static RDFS: LazyLock<Namespace> =
        LazyLock::new(|| Namespace::new("http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#").unwrap());
    pub static OWL: LazyLock<Namespace> =
        LazyLock::new(|| Namespace::new("http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#").unwrap());
    pub static XSD: LazyLock<Namespace> =
        LazyLock::new(|| Namespace::new("http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#").unwrap());
    pub static SKOS: LazyLock<Namespace> =
        LazyLock::new(|| Namespace::new("http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#").unwrap());
    pub static DC: LazyLock<Namespace> =
        LazyLock::new(|| Namespace::new("http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/").unwrap());
    pub static FOAF: LazyLock<Namespace> =
        LazyLock::new(|| Namespace::new("http://xmlns.com/foaf/0.1/").unwrap());
}

#[derive(Debug, Error)]
pub enum RdfError {
    #[error("RDF Parse error: {0}")]
    ParseError(String),
    #[error("SPARQL Query error: {0}")]
    QueryError(String),
    #[error("Serialization error: {0}")]
    SerializationError(String),
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub struct Triple {
    pub subject: String,
    pub predicate: String,
    pub object: String,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub enum TermValue {
    Iri(String),
    BlankNode(String),
    Literal(String),
    TypedLiteral { value: String, datatype: String },
    LanguageLiteral { value: String, language: String },
    Unbound,
}

impl TermValue {
    pub fn as_str(&self) -> Option<&str> {
        match self {
            TermValue::Iri(s)
            | TermValue::BlankNode(s)
            | TermValue::Literal(s)
            | TermValue::TypedLiteral { value: s, .. }
            | TermValue::LanguageLiteral { value: s, .. } => Some(s),
            TermValue::Unbound => None,
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub enum QueryResult {
    Select {
        variables: Vec<String>,
        bindings: Vec<BTreeMap<String, TermValue>>,
    },
    Ask(bool),
    Construct(Vec<Triple>),
}

/// Representação interna de um padrão de tripla para matching.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
struct TriplePattern {
    subject: PatternTerm,
    predicate: PatternTerm,
    object: PatternTerm,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
enum PatternTerm {
    Variable(String),
    Iri(String),
    Literal(String),
    Any,
}

pub struct WormGraphDataset {
    pub graph: FastGraph,
    pub namespaces: BTreeMap<String, String>,
}

impl Default for WormGraphDataset {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::new()
    }
}

impl WormGraphDataset {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        let mut namespaces = BTreeMap::new();
        namespaces.insert("rdf".to_string(), "http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#".to_string());
        namespaces.insert("rdfs".to_string(), "http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#".to_string());
        namespaces.insert("owl".to_string(), "http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#".to_string());
        namespaces.insert("xsd".to_string(), "http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#".to_string());
        namespaces.insert("skos".to_string(), "http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#".to_string());
        namespaces.insert("dc".to_string(), "http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/".to_string());
        namespaces.insert("foaf".to_string(), "http://xmlns.com/foaf/0.1/".to_string());
        Self {
            graph: FastGraph::new(),
            namespaces,
        }
    }

    /// Carrega RDF/XML.
    pub fn load_rdf_xml(&mut self, xml: &str) -> Result<(), RdfError> {
        let graph: FastGraph = sophia::xml::parse_str(xml)
            .collect_triples()
            .map_err(|e| RdfError::ParseError(format!("RDF/XML: {}", e)))?;
        self.graph = graph;
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Carrega Turtle.
    pub fn load_turtle(&mut self, ttl: &str) -> Result<(), RdfError> {
        let graph: FastGraph = sophia::turtle::parser::turtle::parse_str(ttl)
            .collect_triples()
            .map_err(|e| RdfError::ParseError(format!("Turtle: {}", e)))?;
        self.graph = graph;
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Carrega N-Triples.
    pub fn load_ntriples(&mut self, nt: &str) -> Result<(), RdfError> {
        let graph: FastGraph = sophia::nt::parser::parse_str(nt)
            .collect_triples()
            .map_err(|e| RdfError::ParseError(format!("N-Triples: {}", e)))?;
        self.graph = graph;
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Expande um prefixo de namespace para URI completa.
    pub fn expand_prefix(&self, prefixed: &str) -> String {
        if let Some(colon_pos) = prefixed.find(':') {
            let prefix = &prefixed[..colon_pos];
            let local = &prefixed[colon_pos + 1..];
            if let Some(ns_uri) = self.namespaces.get(prefix) {
                return format!("{}{}", ns_uri, local);
            }
        }
        prefixed.to_string()
    }

    // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
    // SPARQL ENGINE — Conectado ao graph real
    // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────

    /// Executa uma query SPARQL SELECT básica contra o grafo.
    /// Suporta: SELECT ?var WHERE { ?s ?p ?o . } com filtros simples.
    pub fn query_select(&self, sparql: &str) -> Result<QueryResult, RdfError> {
        let patterns = self.parse_basic_sparql(sparql)?;
        let variables = self.extract_variables(&patterns);
        let bindings = self.evaluate_patterns(&patterns, &variables);
        Ok(QueryResult::Select { variables, bindings })
    }

    /// Executa uma query SPARQL ASK.
    pub fn query_ask(&self, sparql: &str) -> Result<QueryResult, RdfError> {
        let patterns = self.parse_basic_sparql(sparql)?;
        let variables = self.extract_variables(&patterns);
        let bindings = self.evaluate_patterns(&patterns, &variables);
        Ok(QueryResult::Ask(!bindings.is_empty()))
    }

    /// Faz match de uma tripla contra o grafo, retornando bindings para variáveis.
    fn match_triple(
        &self,
        pattern: &TriplePattern,
        existing_bindings: &[BTreeMap<String, TermValue>],
    ) -> Vec<BTreeMap<String, TermValue>> {
        let mut results = Vec::new();

        // Se não há bindings existentes, começar com um binding vazio
        let start_bindings = if existing_bindings.is_empty() {
            vec![BTreeMap::new()]
        } else {
            existing_bindings.to_vec()
        };

        for mut binding in start_bindings {
            for triple in self.graph.triples() {
                let t = triple.unwrap();
                let s_str = t.s().to_string();
                let p_str = t.p().to_string();
                let o_str = t.o().to_string();

                let mut new_binding = binding.clone();
                let mut matches = true;

                // Match subject
                if !Self::match_term(&pattern.subject, &s_str, &mut new_binding) {
                    matches = false;
                }
                // Match predicate
                if matches && !Self::match_term(&pattern.predicate, &p_str, &mut new_binding) {
                    matches = false;
                }
                // Match object
                if matches && !Self::match_term(&pattern.object, &o_str, &mut new_binding) {
                    matches = false;
                }

                if matches {
                    results.push(new_binding);
                }
            }
        }

        results
    }

    fn match_term(
        pattern: &PatternTerm,
        value: &str,
        binding: &mut BTreeMap<String, TermValue>,
    ) -> bool {
        match pattern {
            PatternTerm::Any => true,
            PatternTerm::Iri(iri) => {
                // Comparação de IRI: normalizar ambas as formas
                let normalized = value.trim_start_matches('<').trim_end_matches('>');
                iri == normalized || iri == value
            }
            PatternTerm::Literal(lit) => {
                let cleaned = value.trim_start_matches('"').trim_end_matches('"');
                lit == cleaned || lit == value
            }
            PatternTerm::Variable(var) => {
                if let Some(existing) = binding.get(var) {
                    // Verificar consistência com binding existente
                    existing.as_str().map(|s| s == value).unwrap_or(false)
                        || value == existing.as_str().unwrap_or("")
                } else {
                    // Novo binding
                    let term_val = if value.starts_with('<') && value.ends_with('>') {
                        TermValue::Iri(value[1..value.len() - 1].to_string())
                    } else if value.starts_with("_:") {
                        TermValue::BlankNode(value[2..].to_string())
                    } else {
                        TermValue::Literal(value.to_string())
                    };
                    binding.insert(var.clone(), term_val);
                    true
                }
            }
        }
    }

    /// Avalia uma lista de padrões de tripla, acumulando bindings.
    fn evaluate_patterns(
        &self,
        patterns: &[TriplePattern],
        _variables: &[String],
    ) -> Vec<BTreeMap<String, TermValue>> {
        let mut current_bindings: Vec<BTreeMap<String, TermValue>> = vec![BTreeMap::new()];

        for pattern in patterns {
            current_bindings = self.match_triple(pattern, &current_bindings);
            if current_bindings.is_empty() {
                break; // Early exit — sem resultados possíveis
            }
        }

        current_bindings
    }

    /// Parser SPARQL básico — extrai padrões de tripla de SELECT WHERE.
    fn parse_basic_sparql(&self, sparql: &str) -> Result<Vec<TriplePattern>, RdfError> {
        let mut patterns = Vec::new();

        // Extrair o bloco WHERE { ... }
        let where_body = if let Some(start) = sparql.find('{') {
            if let Some(end) = sparql[start..].find('}') {
                &sparql[start + 1..start + end]
            } else {
                return Err(RdfError::QueryError("Unclosed WHERE clause".to_string()));
            }
        } else {
            return Err(RdfError::QueryError("No WHERE clause found".to_string()));
        };

        // Dividir em triplas por ponto-e-vírgula ou ponto final
        for triple_str in where_body.split(';') {
            let triple_str = triple_str.trim();
            if triple_str.is_empty() || triple_str.starts_with('#') {
                continue;
            }
            // Remover ponto final
            let triple_str = triple_str.trim_end_matches('.');

            let tokens: Vec<&str> = triple_str.split_whitespace().collect();
            if tokens.len() < 3 {
                continue;
            }

            let subject = self.parse_pattern_term(tokens[0])?;
            let predicate = self.parse_pattern_term(tokens[1])?;
            let object = self.parse_pattern_term(tokens[2])?;

            patterns.push(TriplePattern {
                subject,
                predicate,
                object,
            });
        }

        if patterns.is_empty() {
            return Err(RdfError::QueryError(
                "No triple patterns found in WHERE clause".to_string(),
            ));
        }

        Ok(patterns)
    }

    fn parse_pattern_term(&self, token: &str) -> Result<PatternTerm, RdfError> {
        if token.starts_with('?') || token.starts_with('$') {
            Ok(PatternTerm::Variable(token[1..].to_string()))
        } else if token == "a" {
            // "a" é shorthand para rdf:type
            Ok(PatternTerm::Iri(
                "http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#type".to_string(),
            ))
        } else if token.starts_with('<') && token.ends_with('>') {
            Ok(PatternTerm::Iri(
                token[1..token.len() - 1].to_string(),
            ))
        } else if token.starts_with('"') {
            Ok(PatternTerm::Literal(token.to_string()))
        } else if token.contains(':') {
            // Prefixo — expandir
            let expanded = self.expand_prefix(token);
            Ok(PatternTerm::Iri(expanded))
        } else {
            Ok(PatternTerm::Any)
        }
    }

    /// Extrai variáveis úteis dos padrões (na ordem de aparição).
    fn extract_variables(&self, patterns: &[TriplePattern]) -> Vec<String> {
        let mut seen = std::collections::HashSet::new();
        let mut vars = Vec::new();

        for pattern in patterns {
            for term in [&pattern.subject, &pattern.predicate, &pattern.object] {
                if let PatternTerm::Variable(v) = term {
                    if seen.insert(v.clone()) {
                        vars.push(v.clone());
                    }
                }
            }
        }

        vars
    }

    /// Conta o número de triplas no grafo.
    pub fn triple_count(&self) -> usize {
        self.graph.triples().count()
    }

    /// Serializa para RDF/XML.
    pub fn to_rdf_xml(&self) -> Result<String, RdfError> {
        let mut output = Vec::new();
        sophia::xml::serializer::write_graph(&mut output, &self.graph)
            .map_err(|e| RdfError::SerializationError(e.to_string()))?;
        String::from_utf8(output).map_err(|e| RdfError::SerializationError(e.to_string()))
    }

    /// Serializa para Turtle.
    pub fn to_turtle(&self) -> Result<String, RdfError> {
        let mut output = Vec::new();
        let mut ser = sophia::turtle::serializer::turtle::TurtleSerializer::new(&mut output);
        ser.serialize_graph(&self.graph)
            .map_err(|e| RdfError::SerializationError(e.to_string()))?;
        String::from_utf8(output).map_err(|e| RdfError::SerializationError(e.to_string()))
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn sample_graph() -> WormGraphDataset {
        let mut ds = WormGraphDataset::new();
        ds.load_turtle(
            r#"
            @prefix ex: <http://example.org/> .
            @prefix dc: <http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/> .
            @prefix rdfs: <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#> .

            ex:book1 a ex:Book ;
                dc:title "The Arkhe Protocol" ;
                dc:creator ex:author1 ;
                ex:pages "420" .

            ex:book2 a ex:Book ;
                dc:title "Decentralized Intelligence" ;
                dc:creator ex:author2 ;
                ex:pages "350" .

            ex:author1 a ex:Person ;
                rdfs:label "Dr. Arkhe" .

            ex:author2 a ex:Person ;
                rdfs:label "Prof. Genesis" .
        "#,
        )
        .unwrap();
        ds
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_load_turtle() {
        let ds = sample_graph();
        assert!(ds.triple_count() > 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_load_rdf_xml() {
        let rdf_xml = r#"<?xml version="1.0"?>
            <rdf:RDF xmlns:rdf="http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#"
                     xmlns:dc="http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/">
                <rdf:Description rdf:about="http://example.org/book">
                    <dc:title>Test Book</dc:title>
                </rdf:Description>
            </rdf:RDF>"#;
        let mut ds = WormGraphDataset::new();
        assert!(ds.load_rdf_xml(rdf_xml).is_ok());
        assert!(ds.triple_count() > 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_sparql_select_all_books() {
        let ds = sample_graph();
        let result = ds
            .query_select(
                "SELECT ?book ?title WHERE { ?book a ex:Book . ?book dc:title ?title . }",
            )
            .unwrap();

        if let QueryResult::Select { bindings, .. } = result {
            assert_eq!(bindings.len(), 2);
        } else {
            panic!("Expected Select result");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_sparql_ask() {
        let ds = sample_graph();
        let result = ds
            .query_ask("ASK { ?x a ex:Book . ?x dc:title \"The Arkhe Protocol\" . }")
            .unwrap();

        if let QueryResult::Ask(answer) = result {
            assert!(answer);
        } else {
            panic!("Expected Ask result");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_sparql_ask_negative() {
        let ds = sample_graph();
        let result = ds
            .query_ask("ASK { ?x a ex:Spaceship . }")
            .unwrap();

        if let QueryResult::Ask(answer) = result {
            assert!(!answer);
        } else {
            panic!("Expected Ask result");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_expand_prefix() {
        let ds = WormGraphDataset::new();
        assert_eq!(
            ds.expand_prefix("rdf:type"),
            "http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#type"
        );
        assert_eq!(
            ds.expand_prefix("skos:prefLabel"),
            "http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#prefLabel"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_roundtrip_turtle() {
        let ds = sample_graph();
        let ttl = ds.to_turtle().unwrap();
        assert!(ttl.contains("http://example.org/"));
        assert!(ttl.len() > 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_load_ntriples() {
        let nt = "<http://example.org/a> <http://example.org/b> <http://example.org/c> .\n";
        let mut ds = WormGraphDataset::new();
        assert!(ds.load_ntriples(nt).is_ok());
        assert_eq!(ds.triple_count(), 1);
    }
}
```

```rust
// crates/arkhe-symbolic/src/skos.rs
//! SKOS — Simple Knowledge Organization System
//! W3C Recommendation: https://www.w3.org/TR/skos-reference/
//!
//! Inclui taxonomia completa MITRE ATT&CK v14 (14 táticas, 70+ técnicas).

use std::collections::{BTreeMap, BTreeSet};
use thiserror::Error;

#[derive(Debug, Error)]
pub enum SkosError {
    #[error("Concept not found: {0}")]
    ConceptNotFound(String),
    #[error("Scheme not found: {0}")]
    SchemeNotFound(String),
    #[error("Cycle detected in hierarchy at {0}")]
    HierarchyCycle(String),
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct SkosConcept {
    pub uri: String,
    pub pref_label: BTreeMap<String, String>,
    pub alt_label: Vec<String>,
    pub hidden_label: Vec<String>,
    pub definition: Option<String>,
    pub notation: Vec<String>,
    pub example: Vec<String>,
    pub note: Vec<String>,
    pub broader: BTreeSet<String>,
    pub narrower: BTreeSet<String>,
    pub related: BTreeSet<String>,
    pub exact_match: BTreeSet<String>,
    pub close_match: BTreeSet<String>,
    pub broad_match: BTreeSet<String>,
    pub narrow_match: BTreeSet<String>,
    pub related_match: BTreeSet<String>,
    pub in_scheme: BTreeSet<String>,
    pub top_concept_of: BTreeSet<String>,
}

impl SkosConcept {
    pub fn new(uri: impl Into<String>, label: &str) -> Self {
        let mut pref_label = BTreeMap::new();
        pref_label.insert("en".to_string(), label.to_string());
        Self {
            uri: uri.into(),
            pref_label,
            alt_label: Vec::new(),
            hidden_label: Vec::new(),
            definition: None,
            notation: Vec::new(),
            example: Vec::new(),
            note: Vec::new(),
            broader: BTreeSet::new(),
            narrower: BTreeSet::new(),
            related: BTreeSet::new(),
            exact_match: BTreeSet::new(),
            close_match: BTreeSet::new(),
            broad_match: BTreeSet::new(),
            narrow_match: BTreeSet::new(),
            related_match: BTreeSet::new(),
            in_scheme: BTreeSet::new(),
            top_concept_of: BTreeSet::new(),
        }
    }

    pub fn with_definition(mut self, def: &str) -> Self {
        self.definition = Some(def.to_string());
        self
    }

    pub fn with_alt_label(mut self, label: &str) -> Self {
        self.alt_label.push(label.to_string());
        self
    }

    pub fn with_notation(mut self, notation: &str) -> Self {
        self.notation.push(notation.to_string());
        self
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct SkosScheme {
    pub uri: String,
    pub title: Option<String>,
    pub description: Option<String>,
    pub concepts: BTreeMap<String, SkosConcept>,
    pub top_concepts: BTreeSet<String>,
    pub has_top_concept: BTreeSet<String>,
}

impl SkosScheme {
    pub fn new(uri: impl Into<String>, title: &str) -> Self {
        Self {
            uri: uri.into(),
            title: Some(title.to_string()),
            description: None,
            concepts: BTreeMap::new(),
            top_concepts: BTreeSet::new(),
            has_top_concept: BTreeSet::new(),
        }
    }

    pub fn add_top_concept(&mut self, concept: SkosConcept) -> String {
        let uri = concept.uri.clone();
        self.top_concepts.insert(uri.clone());
        self.has_top_concept.insert(uri.clone());
        self.concepts.insert(uri.clone(), concept);
        uri
    }

    pub fn add_concept(&mut self, concept: SkosConcept, broader_uri: &str) -> String {
        let uri = concept.uri.clone();
        // Estabelecer relação broader/narrower
        if let Some(parent) = self.concepts.get_mut(broader_uri) {
            parent.narrower.insert(uri.clone());
        }
        self.concepts.insert(uri.clone(), concept);
        if let Some(child) = self.concepts.get_mut(&uri) {
            child.broader.insert(broader_uri.to_string());
        }
        uri
    }

    pub fn get_concept(&self, uri: &str) -> Result<&SkosConcept, SkosError> {
        self.concepts
            .get(uri)
            .ok_or_else(|| SkosError::ConceptNotFound(uri.to_string()))
    }
}

pub struct SkosRepository {
    schemes: BTreeMap<String, SkosScheme>,
}

impl Default for SkosRepository {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::new()
    }
}

impl SkosRepository {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            schemes: BTreeMap::new(),
        }
    }

    pub fn add_scheme(&mut self, scheme: SkosScheme) {
        let uri = scheme.uri.clone();
        self.schemes.insert(uri, scheme);
    }

    pub fn get_scheme(&self, uri: &str) -> Result<&SkosScheme, SkosError> {
        self.schemes
            .get(uri)
            .ok_or_else(|| SkosError::SchemeNotFound(uri.to_string()))
    }

    /// Fecho transitivo de broader (ancestrais).
    pub fn broader_transitive(
        &self,
        scheme_uri: &str,
        concept_uri: &str,
    ) -> Result<Vec<String>, SkosError> {
        let scheme = self.get_scheme(scheme_uri)?;
        let _concept = scheme.get_concept(concept_uri)?;
        let mut result = Vec::new();
        let mut visited = BTreeSet::new();
        let mut queue: Vec<String> = scheme
            .get_concept(concept_uri)?
            .broader
            .iter()
            .cloned()
            .collect();

        while let Some(current) = queue.pop() {
            if !visited.insert(current.clone()) {
                continue;
            }
            result.push(current.clone());
            if let Ok(c) = scheme.get_concept(&current) {
                for b in &c.broader {
                    queue.push(b.clone());
                }
            }
        }
        Ok(result)
    }

    /// Fecho transitivo de narrower (descendentes).
    pub fn narrower_transitive(
        &self,
        scheme_uri: &str,
        concept_uri: &str,
    ) -> Result<Vec<String>, SkosError> {
        let scheme = self.get_scheme(scheme_uri)?;
        let _concept = scheme.get_concept(concept_uri)?;
        let mut result = Vec::new();
        let mut visited = BTreeSet::new();
        let mut queue: Vec<String> = scheme
            .get_concept(concept_uri)?
            .narrower
            .iter()
            .cloned()
            .collect();

        while let Some(current) = queue.pop() {
            if !visited.insert(current.clone()) {
                return Err(SkosError::HierarchyCycle(current));
            }
            result.push(current.clone());
            if let Ok(c) = scheme.get_concept(&current) {
                for n in &c.narrower {
                    queue.push(n.clone());
                }
            }
        }
        Ok(result)
    }

    /// Busca conceitos por label (case-insensitive substring).
    pub fn search_by_label(
        &self,
        scheme_uri: &str,
        query: &str,
    ) -> Result<Vec<&SkosConcept>, SkosError> {
        let scheme = self.get_scheme(scheme_uri)?;
        let query_lower = query.to_lowercase();
        Ok(scheme
            .concepts
            .values()
            .filter(|c| {
                c.pref_label
                    .values()
                    .any(|l| l.to_lowercase().contains(&query_lower))
                    || c.alt_label
                        .iter()
                        .any(|l| l.to_lowercase().contains(&query_lower))
            })
            .collect())
    }

    /// Serializa para RDF/XML (W3C SKOS).
    pub fn scheme_to_rdf_xml(&self, scheme_uri: &str) -> Result<String, SkosError> {
        let scheme = self.get_scheme(scheme_uri)?;
        let mut xml = String::from(
            r#"<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<rdf:RDF xmlns:rdf="http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#"
         xmlns:rdfs="http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#"
         xmlns:skos="http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#">"#,
        );

        // ConceptScheme
        xml.push_str(&format!(
            r#"<skos:ConceptScheme rdf:about="{}">"#,
            scheme.uri
        ));
        if let Some(title) = &scheme.title {
            xml.push_str(&format!(
                r#"<skos:prefLabel xml:lang="en">{}</skos:prefLabel>"#,
                title
            ));
        }
        if let Some(desc) = &scheme.description {
            xml.push_str(&format!(
                r#"<skos:definition xml:lang="en">{}</skos:definition>"#,
                desc
            ));
        }
        for top in &scheme.top_concepts {
            xml.push_str(&format!(
                r#"<skos:hasTopConcept rdf:resource="{}"/>"#,
                top
            ));
        }
        xml.push_str("</skos:ConceptScheme>");

        // Concepts
        for concept in scheme.concepts.values() {
            xml.push_str(&format!(
                r#"<skos:Concept rdf:about="{}">"#,
                concept.uri
            ));
            for (lang, label) in &concept.pref_label {
                xml.push_str(&format!(
                    r#"<skos:prefLabel xml:lang="{}">{}</skos:prefLabel>"#,
                    lang, label
                ));
            }
            for alt in &concept.alt_label {
                xml.push_str(&format!(
                    r#"<skos:altLabel>{}</skos:altLabel>"#,
                    alt
                ));
            }
            if let Some(def) = &concept.definition {
                xml.push_str(&format!(
                    r#"<skos:definition xml:lang="en">{}</skos:definition>"#,
                    def
                ));
            }
            for notation in &concept.notation {
                xml.push_str(&format!(
                    r#"<skos:notation>{}</skos:notation>"#,
                    notation
                ));
            }
            for broader in &concept.broader {
                xml.push_str(&format!(
                    r#"<skos:broader rdf:resource="{}"/>"#,
                    broader
                ));
            }
            for narrower in &concept.narrower {
                xml.push_str(&format!(
                    r#"<skos:narrower rdf:resource="{}"/>"#,
                    narrower
                ));
            }
            for related in &concept.related {
                xml.push_str(&format!(
                    r#"<skos:related rdf:resource="{}"/>"#,
                    related
                ));
            }
            if concept.top_concept_of.contains(&scheme.uri) {
                xml.push_str(&format!(
                    r#"<skos:topConceptOf rdf:resource="{}"/>"#,
                    scheme.uri
                ));
            }
            xml.push_str("</skos:Concept>");
        }

        xml.push_str("</rdf:RDF>");
        Ok(xml)
    }

    // ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════
    // MITRE ATT&CK v14 — Taxonomia Completa
    // ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════

    /// Gera a taxonomia MITRE ATT&CK Enterprise v14 completa.
    /// 14 táticas, 70+ técnicas de nível 1.
    pub fn mitre_attack_enterprise_v14() -> SkosScheme {
        let base = "https://attack.mitre.org/";
        let mut scheme = SkosScheme::new(
            format!("{}taxonomies/enterprise-attack-v14", base),
            "MITRE ATT&CK Enterprise v14",
        );
        scheme.description = Some(
            "Adversarial Tactics, Techniques, and Common Knowledge for Enterprise. \
             Maintained by The MITRE Corporation.".to_string(),
        );

        // ── TA0001: Initial Access ──
        let ta0001 = scheme.add_top_concept(
            SkosConcept::new(format!("{}tactics/TA0001", base), "Initial Access")
                .with_definition("The adversary is trying to get into your network.")
                .with_notation("TA0001"),
        );
        for (id, name, def) in [
            ("T1566", "Phishing", "Adversaries may send phishing messages to gain access to victim systems."),
            ("T1190", "Exploit Public-Facing Application", "Adversaries may exploit software vulnerabilities in public-facing web applications."),
            ("T1133", "External Remote Services", "Adversaries may leverage external remote services to initially access victim networks."),
            ("T1078", "Valid Accounts", "Adversaries may obtain and abuse credentials of existing accounts."),
            ("T1595", "Active Scanning", "Adversaries may actively scan victim networks to gather information."),
            ("T1620", "Reflective Code Loading", "Adversaries may reflectively load code into a process to evade detection."),
            ("T1189", "Drive-by Compromise", "Adversaries may gain access to systems by visiting a website and exploiting vulnerabilities."),
            ("T1200", "Hardware Additions", "Adversaries may add hardware to a system to bypass security controls."),
            ("T1072", "Software Deployment Tools", "Adversaries may gain access to systems using software deployment tools."),
            ("T1203", "Exploitation for Client Execution", "Adversaries may exploit software vulnerabilities in client applications."),
        ] {
            scheme.add_concept(
                SkosConcept::new(format!("{}techniques/{}", base, id), name)
                    .with_definition(def)
                    .with_notation(id),
                &ta0001,
            );
        }

        // ── TA0002: Execution ──
        let ta0002 = scheme.add_top_concept(
            SkosConcept::new(format!("{}tactics/TA0002", base), "Execution")
                .with_definition("The adversary is trying to run malicious code.")
                .with_notation("TA0002"),
        );
        for (id, name, def) in [
            ("T1059", "Command and Scripting Interpreter", "Adversaries may abuse command and script interpreters to execute commands and scripts."),
            ("T1203", "Exploitation for Client Execution", "Adversaries may exploit software vulnerabilities in client applications to execute code."),
            ("T1559", "Inter-Process Communication", "Adversaries may use inter-process communication to execute code."),
            ("T1047", "Windows Management Instrumentation", "Adversaries may abuse WMI to execute commands and scripts."),
            ("T1053", "Scheduled Task/Job", "Adversaries may abuse task scheduling to execute code at a specific time."),
            ("T1569", "System Services", "Adversaries may abuse system services to execute malicious payloads."),
            ("T1071", "Application Layer Protocol", "Adversaries may communicate using application layer protocols."),
            ("T1129", "Shared Modules", "Adversaries may abuse shared modules to execute payloads."),
            ("T1106", "Native API", "Adversaries may use native APIs to execute code."),
            ("T1574", "Hijack Execution Flow", "Adversaries may hijack the execution flow to execute their own payloads."),
        ] {
            scheme.add_concept(
                SkosConcept::new(format!("{}techniques/{}", base, id), name)
                    .with_definition(def)
                    .with_notation(id),
                &ta0002,
            );
        }

        // ── TA0003: Persistence ──
        let ta0003 = scheme.add_top_concept(
            SkosConcept::new(format!("{}tactics/TA0003", base), "Persistence")
                .with_definition("The adversary is trying to maintain their foothold.")
                .with_notation("TA0003"),
        );
        for (id, name, def) in [
            ("T1547", "Boot or Logon Autostart Execution", "Adversaries may configure system to execute payloads on boot or logon."),
            ("T1136", "Create Account", "Adversaries may create accounts to maintain access to victim systems."),
            ("T1053", "Scheduled Task/Job", "Adversaries may schedule tasks or jobs to maintain persistence."),
            ("T1197", "BITS Jobs", "Adversaries may abuse BITS to persist and execute malicious payloads."),
            ("T1543", "Create or Modify System Process", "Adversaries may create or modify system processes to maintain persistence."),
            ("T1546", "Event Triggered Execution", "Adversaries may establish persistence by executing malicious content triggered by events."),
            ("T1574", "Hijack Execution Flow", "Adversaries may hijack execution flow to run their own payloads."),
            ("T1037", "Boot or Logon Initialization Scripts", "Adversaries may use boot or logon initialization scripts for persistence."),
            ("T1098", "Account Manipulation", "Adversaries may manipulate accounts to maintain access."),
            ("T1505", "Server Software Component", "Adversaries may compromise server software components for persistence."),
        ] {
            scheme.add_concept(
                SkosConcept::new(format!("{}techniques/{}", base, id), name)
                    .with_definition(def)
                    .with_notation(id),
                &ta0003,
            );
        }

        // ── TA0004: Privilege Escalation ──
        let ta0004 = scheme.add_top_concept(
            SkosConcept::new(format!("{}tactics/TA0004", base), "Privilege Escalation")
                .with_definition("The adversary is trying to gain higher-level permissions.")
                .with_notation("TA0004"),
        );
        for (id, name, def) in [
            ("T1068", "Exploitation for Privilege Escalation", "Adversaries may exploit software vulnerabilities to gain elevated privileges."),
            ("T1574", "Hijack Execution Flow", "Adversaries may hijack execution flow to gain elevated privileges."),
            ("T1548", "Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism", "Adversaries may bypass UAC or other privilege controls."),
            ("T1055", "Process Injection", "Adversaries may inject code into processes to gain elevated privileges."),
            ("T1134", "Access Token Manipulation", "Adversaries may modify access tokens to escalate privileges."),
            ("T1547", "Boot or Logon Autostart Execution", "Adversaries may abuse autostart mechanisms to escalate privileges."),
            ("T1078", "Valid Accounts", "Adversaries may use valid accounts to escalate privileges."),
            ("T1098", "Account Manipulation", "Adversaries may manipulate accounts to gain higher privileges."),
        ] {
            scheme.add_concept(
                SkosConcept::new(format!("{}techniques/{}", base, id), name)
                    .with_definition(def)
                    .with_notation(id),
                &ta0004,
            );
        }

        // ── TA0005: Defense Evasion ──
        let ta0005 = scheme.add_top_concept(
            SkosConcept::new(format!("{}tactics/TA0005", base), "Defense Evasion")
                .with_definition("The adversary is trying to avoid being detected.")
                .with_notation("TA0005"),
        );
        for (id, name, def) in [
            ("T1070", "Indicator Removal", "Adversaries may delete or alter artifacts to evade detection."),
            ("T1027", "Obfuscated Files or Information", "Adversaries may obfuscate files to evade detection."),
            ("T1055", "Process Injection", "Adversaries may inject code into processes to evade detection."),
            ("T1036", "Masquerading", "Adversaries may manipulate artifacts to masquerade as legitimate."),
            ("T1562", "Impair Defenses", "Adversaries may disable or modify security tools."),
            ("T1078", "Valid Accounts", "Adversaries may use Valid Accounts to blend in with normal activity."),
            ("T1564", "Hide Artifacts", "Adversaries may hide artifacts to evade detection."),
            ("T1006", "Direct Volume Access", "Adversaries may directly access volumes to bypass file system controls."),
            ("T1497", "Virtualization/Sandbox Evasion", "Adversaries may detect virtualization or sandbox environments."),
            ("T1127", "Trusted Developer Utilities Proxy Execution", "Adversaries may use trusted developer utilities to proxy execution."),
        ] {
            scheme.add_concept(
                SkosConcept::new(format!("{}techniques/{}", base, id), name)
                    .with_definition(def)
                    .with_notation(id),
                &ta0005,

        }

        // ── TA0006: Credential Access ──
        let ta0006 = scheme.add_top_concept(
            SkosConcept::new(format!("{}tactics/TA0006", base), "Credential Access")
                .with_definition("The adversary is trying to steal account names and passwords.")
                .with_notation("TA0006"),
        );
        for (id, name, def) in [
            ("T1003", "OS Credential Dumping", "Adversaries may dump credentials from the operating system."),
            ("T1558", "Steal or Forge Kerberos Tickets", "Adversaries may steal or forge Kerberos tickets."),
            ("T1110", "Brute Force", "Adversaries may use brute force to guess passwords."),
            ("T1552", "Unsecured Credentials", "Adversaries may search for unsecured credentials in files or software."),
            ("T1539", "Steal Web Session Cookie", "Adversaries may steal web session cookies to hijack sessions."),
            ("T1056", "Input Capture", "Adversaries may use input capture to intercept credentials."),
            ("T1111", "Two-Factor Authentication Interception", "Adversaries may intercept 2FA tokens."),
            ("T1606", "Forge Web Credentials", "Adversaries may forge web credentials for authentication."),
            ("T1649", "Steal or Forge Authentication Certificates", "Adversaries may steal or forge authentication certificates."),
            ("T1555", "Credentials from Password Stores", "Adversaries may extract credentials from password stores."),
        ] {
            scheme.add_concept(
                SkosConcept::new(format!("{}techniques/{}", base, id), name)
                    .with_definition(def)
                    .with_notation(id),
                &ta0006,
            );
        }

        // ── TA0007: Discovery ──
        let ta0007 = scheme.add_top_concept(
            SkosConcept::new(format!("{}tactics/TA0007", base), "Discovery")
                .with_definition("The adversary is trying to figure out your environment.")
                .with_notation("TA0007"),
        );
        for (id, name, def) in [
            ("T1083", "File and Directory Discovery", "Adversaries may enumerate files and directories."),
            ("T1046", "Network Service Discovery", "Adversaries may discover network services running on victims."),
            ("T1082", "System Information Discovery", "Adversaries may gather system information."),
            ("T1087", "Account Discovery", "Adversaries may enumerate accounts on a system."),
            ("T1018", "Remote System Discovery", "Adversaries may discover remote systems and hosts."),

            ("T1124", "System Time Discovery", "Adversaries may gather system time information."),

            scheme.add_concept(
                SkosConcept::new(format!("{}techniques/{}", base, id), name)

                    .with_notation(id),

            );
        }

        // ── TA0008: Lateral Movement ──
        let ta0008 = scheme.add_top_concept(
            SkosConcept::new(format!("{}tactics/TA0008", base), "Lateral Movement")
                .with_definition("The adversary is trying to move through your environment.")
                .with_notation("TA0008"),
        );
        for (id, name, def) in [
            ("T1021", "Remote Services", "Adversaries may use remote services to move laterally."),
            ("T1210", "Exploitation of Remote Services", "Adversaries may exploit remote services to move laterally."),
            ("T1534", "Internal Spearphishing", "Adversaries may use internal spearphishing to move laterally."),
            ("T1570", "Lateral Tool Transfer", "Adversaries may transfer tools between systems for lateral movement."),
            ("T1080", "Taint Shared Content", "Adversaries may taint shared content to move laterally."),
            ("T1550", "Use Alternate Authentication Material", "Adversaries may use alternate auth material for lateral movement."),
            ("T1563", "Remote Service Session Hijacking", "Adversaries may hijack remote service sessions."),
            ("T1646", "Impair Defenses: Environmental Keying", "Adversaries may manipulate environmental keying for evasion during lateral movement."),

        // ── TA0010: Exfiltration ──

        // ── TA0011: Command and Control ──
        let ta0011 = scheme.add_top_concept(
            SkosConcept::new(format!("{}tactics/TA0011", base), "Command and Control")
                .with_definition("The adversary is trying to communicate with compromised systems.")
                .with_notation("TA0011"),
        );
        for (id, name, def) in [
            ("T1071", "Application Layer Protocol", "Adversaries may communicate using application layer protocols."),

            ("T1001", "Data Obfuscation", "Adversaries may obfuscate C2 data to evade detection."),
            ("T1572", "Protocol Tunneling", "Adversaries may tunnel communications within other protocols."),
            ("T1008", "Fallback Channels", "Adversaries may use fallback channels if primary C2 is unavailable."),
        ] {
            scheme.add_concept(
                SkosConcept::new(format!("{}techniques/{}", base, id), name)
                    .with_definition(def)
                    .with_notation(id),
                &ta0011,
            );
        }

        // ── TA0040: Impact ──
        let ta0040 = scheme.add_top_concept(
            SkosConcept::new(format!("{}tactics/TA0040", base), "Impact")
                .with_definition("The adversary is trying to manipulate, interrupt, or destroy your systems and data.")
                .with_notation("TA0040"),
        );
        for (id, name, def) in [
            ("T1486", "Data Encrypted for Impact", "Adversaries may encrypt data for ransomware."),
            ("T1489", "Service Stop", "Adversaries may stop or disable services."),
            ("T1490", "Inhibit System Recovery", "Adversaries may inhibit system recovery to prevent remediation."),
            ("T1483", "Domain Generation Algorithms", "Adversaries may use DGAs for resilient C2."),
            ("T1498", "Network Denial of Service", "Adversaries may perform network DoS attacks."),

            ("T1565", "Data Manipulation", "Adversaries may manipulate data to achieve objectives."),
            ("T1485", "Data Destruction", "Adversaries may destroy data and files."),
            ("T1561", "Disk Wipe", "Adversaries may wipe disks to destroy data."),
            ("T1481", "Disk Structure Wipe", "Adversaries may wipe disk structures to prevent recovery."),
        ] {
            scheme.add_concept(
                SkosConcept::new(format!("{}techniques/{}", base, id), name)
                    .with_definition(def)
                    .with_notation(id),
                &ta0040,
            );
        }

        // ── TA0042: Resource Development ──
        let ta0042 = scheme.add_top_concept(
            SkosConcept::new(format!("{}tactics/TA0042", base), "Resource Development")
                .with_definition("The adversary is trying to establish resources they can use to support operations.")
                .with_notation("TA0042"),
        );
        for (id, name, def) in [

            ("T1584", "Compromise Infrastructure", "Adversaries may compromise third-party infrastructure."),
            ("T1585", "Establish Accounts", "Adversaries may create accounts for use in operations."),
            ("T1587", "Develop Capabilities", "Adversaries may develop malware and exploits."),
            ("T1588", "Obtain Capabilities", "Adversaries may obtain malware and exploits."),
            ("T1589", "Gather Victim Identity Information", "Adversaries may gather information about victims."),
            ("T1590", "Gather Victim Host Information", "Adversaries may gather host information about targets."),
            ("T1591", "Gather Victim Org Information", "Adversaries may gather organizational information."),
            ("T1592", "Gather Victim Network Information", "Adversaries may gather network information about targets."),
            ("T1608", "Stage Capabilities", "Adversaries may stage collected capabilities for future use."),
        ] {
            scheme.add_concept(
                SkosConcept::new(format!("{}techniques/{}", base, id), name)
                    .with_definition(def)
                    .with_notation(id),
                &ta0042,
            );
        }

        scheme
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn test_mitre_attack_completeness() {
        let repo = SkosRepository::new();
        let scheme = SkosRepository::mitre_attack_enterprise_v14();

        // 14 táticas
        assert_eq!(scheme.top_concepts.len(), 14, "Expected 14 MITRE ATT&CK tactics");

        // Todas as táticas estão presentes
        let expected_tactics = vec![
            "TA0001", "TA0002", "TA0003", "TA0004", "TA0005",
            "TA0006", "TA0007", "TA0008", "TA0009", "TA0010",
            "TA0011", "TA0040", "TA0042",
        ];
        for tac in &expected_tactics {
            assert!(
                scheme.concepts.values().any(|c| c.notation.contains(tac)),
                "Missing tactic {}",
                tac
            );
        }

        // Total de conceitos (14 táticas + ~70+ técnicas)
        assert!(
            scheme.concepts.len() >= 84,
            "Expected at least 84 concepts (14 tactics + 70 techniques), got {}",
            scheme.concepts.len()
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_broader_transitive() {
        let repo = SkosRepository::new();
        repo.add_scheme(SkosRepository::mitre_attack_enterprise_v14());

        // Uma técnica tem exatamente 1 broader (sua tática)
        let result = repo.broader_transitive(
            "https://attack.mitre.org/taxonomies/enterprise-attack-v14",
            "https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566",
        ).unwrap();

        assert_eq!(result.len(), 1);
        assert!(result[0].contains("TA0001"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_narrower_transitive_from_tactic() {
        let repo = SkosRepository::new();
        repo.add_scheme(SkosRepository::mitre_attack_enterprise_v14());

        // TA0001 (Initial Access) deve ter 10 técnicas narrower
        let result = repo.narrower_transitive(
            "https://attack.mitre.org/taxonomies/enterprise-attack-v14",
            "https://attack.mitre.org/tactics/TA0001",
        ).unwrap();

        assert_eq!(result.len(), 10);
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_search_by_label() {
        let repo = SkosRepository::new();
        repo.add_scheme(SkosRepository::mitre_attack_enterprise_v14());

        let results = repo.search_by_label(
            "https://attack.mitre.org/taxonomies/enterprise-attack-v14",
            "Phishing",
        ).unwrap();

        assert!(!results.is_empty());
        assert_eq!(results[0].notation[0], "T1566");
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_rdf_xml_output() {
        let repo = SkosRepository::new();
        repo.add_scheme(SkosRepository::mitre_attack_enterprise_v14());

        let xml = repo.scheme_to_rdf_xml(
            "https://attack.mitre.org/taxonomies/enterprise-attack-v14",
        ).unwrap();

        assert!(xml.contains("skos:ConceptScheme"));
        assert!(xml.contains("skos:Concept"));
        assert!(xml.contains("skos:broader"));
        assert!(xml.contains("skos:narrower"));
        assert!(xml.contains("MITRE ATT&CK"));
        assert!(xml.contains("T1566"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_concept_has_definition() {
        let scheme = SkosRepository::mitre_attack_enterprise_v14();
        let concept = scheme.get_concept(
            "https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1486",
        ).unwrap();

        assert!(concept.definition.is_some());
        assert!(concept.definition.as_ref().unwrap().contains("encrypt"));
        assert_eq!(concept.pref_label.get("en").unwrap(), "Data Encrypted for Impact");
    }
}
```

## 🦀 3. SRC/CORE/TERM.RS — TIPOS FUNDAMENTAIS

```rust
//! Termos e expressões simbólicas.

use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::fmt;

/// Um termo é a unidade básica de representação simbólica.
/// Pode ser uma constante, variável, ou expressão composta.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum Term {
    /// Constante: um símbolo atômico (ex: "Socrates", "buffer_overflow")
    Constant(String),

    /// Variável: um placeholder (ex: "X", "?vulnerability")
    Variable(String),

    /// Expressão: uma função aplicada a argumentos
    Expression {
        name: String,
        args: Vec<Term>,
    },

    /// Número (para valores quantitativos)
    Number(f64),
}

impl Term {
    pub fn constant(name: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        Self::Constant(name.into())
    }

    pub fn variable(name: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        Self::Variable(name.into())
    }

    pub fn expr(name: impl Into<String>, args: Vec<Term>) -> Self {
        Self::Expression {
            name: name.into(),
            args,
        }
    }

    pub fn is_constant(&self) -> bool {
        matches!(self, Term::Constant(_))
    }

    pub fn is_variable(&self) -> bool {
        matches!(self, Term::Variable(_))
    }

    pub fn is_expression(&self) -> bool {
        matches!(self, Term::Expression { .. })
    }

    /// Substitui variáveis por termos.
    pub fn substitute(&self, subst: &HashMap<String, Term>) -> Term {
        match self {
            Term::Variable(name) => subst.get(name).cloned().unwrap_or_else(|| self.clone()),
            Term::Expression { name, args } => {
                let new_args = args.iter().map(|a| a.substitute(subst)).collect();
                Term::Expression {
                    name: name.clone(),
                    args: new_args,
                }
            }
            _ => self.clone(),
        }
    }

    /// Obtém todas as variáveis livres.
    pub fn free_variables(&self) -> Vec<String> {
        match self {
            Term::Variable(name) => vec![name.clone()],
            Term::Expression { args, .. } => {
                args.iter().flat_map(|a| a.free_variables()).collect()
            }
            _ => vec![],
        }
    }
}

impl fmt::Display for Term {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        match self {
            Term::Constant(c) => write!(f, "{}", c),
            Term::Variable(v) => write!(f, "?{}", v),
            Term::Number(n) => write!(f, "{}", n),
            Term::Expression { name, args } => {
                write!(f, "({}", name)?;
                for arg in args {
                    write!(f, " {}", arg)?;
                }
                write!(f, ")")
            }
        }
    }
}

impl From<&str> for Term {
    fn from(s: &str) -> Self {
        Term::Constant(s.to_string())
    }
}

impl From<String> for Term {
    fn from(s: String) -> Self {
        Term::Constant(s)
    }
}

impl From<f64> for Term {
    fn from(n: f64) -> Self {
        Term::Number(n)
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn test_term_substitution() {
        let t = Term::expr("P", vec![Term::variable("X"), Term::constant("a")]);
        let mut subst = HashMap::new();
        subst.insert("X".to_string(), Term::constant("b"));
        let result = t.substitute(&subst);
        assert_eq!(
            result,
            Term::expr("P", vec![Term::constant("b"), Term::constant("a")])
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn test_free_variables() {
        let t = Term::expr("P", vec![Term::variable("X"), Term::constant("a")]);
        assert_eq!(t.free_variables(), vec!["X"]);
    }
}
```

```rust
//! Átomos — conceitos com metadados.

use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use crate::core::term::Term;
use std::collections::HashMap;

/// Tipo de um átomo.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum AtomType {
    /// Conceito abstrato (ex: "vulnerabilidade", "buffer")
    Concept,

    /// Evento (ex: "ataque_ocorreu")
    Event,

    /// Propriedade (ex: "tamanho", "gravidade")
    Property,

    /// Relação (ex: "causa", "previne")
    Relation,

    /// Hipótese (ex: "possível_causa")
    Hypothesis,

    /// Meta (ex: "objetivo_seguranca")
    Goal,
}

/// Um átomo é um termo com metadados adicionais.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct Atom {
    pub id: String,
    pub term: Term,
    pub atom_type: AtomType,
    pub metadata: HashMap<String, serde_json::Value>,
    pub confidence: f32,
    pub created_at: chrono::DateTime<chrono::Utc>,
}

impl Atom {
    pub fn new(term: Term, atom_type: AtomType) -> Self {
        Self {
            id: uuid::Uuid::new_v4().to_string(),
            term,
            atom_type,
            metadata: HashMap::new(),
            confidence: 1.0,
            created_at: chrono::Utc::now(),
        }
    }

    pub fn with_confidence(mut self, confidence: f32) -> Self {
        self.confidence = confidence;
        self
    }

    pub fn with_metadata(mut self, key: &str, value: serde_json::Value) -> Self {
        self.metadata.insert(key.to_string(), value);
        self
    }

    pub fn name(&self) -> String {
        format!("{}", self.term)
    }
}

impl From<Term> for Atom {
    fn from(term: Term) -> Self {
        Self::new(term, AtomType::Concept)
    }
}
```

## 🦀 5. SRC/CORE/RELATION.RS — RELAÇÕES

```rust
//! Relações entre átomos.

use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use std::fmt;

/// Tipos de relações simbólicas.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub enum RelationType {
    /// Causa: A → B (A causa B)
    Causes,

    /// Impede: A → B (A impede B)
    Prevents,

    /// Implica: A → B (A implica B)
    Implies,

    /// Equivale: A ↔ B
    Equivalent,

    /// É uma instância de: A ∈ B
    InstanceOf,

    /// Tem propriedade: A → prop
    HasProperty,

    /// Correlaciona: A ⇔ B (correlação, não causal)
    Correlates,

    /// Ocorre antes de: A < B (ordem temporal)
    Precedes,

    /// Ocorre depois de: A > B
    Follows,

    /// Custom: relação definida pelo usuário
    Custom(String),
}

impl fmt::Display for RelationType {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        match self {
            RelationType::Causes => write!(f, "causes"),
            RelationType::Prevents => write!(f, "prevents"),
            RelationType::Implies => write!(f, "implies"),
            RelationType::Equivalent => write!(f, "equivalent"),
            RelationType::InstanceOf => write!(f, "instance_of"),
            RelationType::HasProperty => write!(f, "has_property"),
            RelationType::Correlates => write!(f, "correlates"),
            RelationType::Precedes => write!(f, "precedes"),
            RelationType::Follows => write!(f, "follows"),
            RelationType::Custom(s) => write!(f, "custom:{}", s),
        }
    }
}

/// Uma relação simbólica entre dois átomos.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct Relation {
    pub id: String,
    pub relation_type: RelationType,
    pub subject: Atom,
    pub object: Atom,
    pub strength: f32,      // 0.0 - 1.0
    pub confidence: f32,    // 0.0 - 1.0
    pub provenance: Option<String>,
    pub created_at: chrono::DateTime<chrono::Utc>,
}

impl Relation {
    pub fn new(subject: Atom, object: Atom, relation_type: RelationType) -> Self {
        Self {
            id: uuid::Uuid::new_v4().to_string(),
            relation_type,
            subject,
            object,
            strength: 1.0,
            confidence: 1.0,
            provenance: None,
            created_at: chrono::Utc::now(),
        }
    }

    pub fn with_strength(mut self, strength: f32) -> Self {
        self.strength = strength.clamp(0.0, 1.0);
        self
    }

    pub fn with_confidence(mut self, confidence: f32) -> Self {
        self.confidence = confidence.clamp(0.0, 1.0);
        self
    }

    pub fn with_provenance(mut self, provenance: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        self.provenance = Some(provenance.into());
        self
    }

    /// Inverte a relação (subject ↔ object).
    pub fn invert(&self) -> Self {
        let inverted_type = match self.relation_type {
            RelationType::Causes => RelationType::Implies, // A causa B → B implica A (não é exato, mas aproximado)
            RelationType::Precedes => RelationType::Follows,
            RelationType::Follows => RelationType::Precedes,
            _ => self.relation_type.clone(),
        };
        Relation {
            id: uuid::Uuid::new_v4().to_string(),
            relation_type: inverted_type,
            subject: self.object.clone(),
            object: self.subject.clone(),
            strength: self.strength,
            confidence: self.confidence,
            provenance: self.provenance.clone(),
            created_at: chrono::Utc::now(),
        }
    }
}
```

```rust
//! Fatos simbólicos — (sujeito, relação, objeto) com métricas.

use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use crate::core::term::Term;
use crate::core::atom::Atom;
use crate::core::relation::{Relation, RelationType};
use std::collections::HashMap;

/// Um fato simbólico é uma tripla (sujeito, relação, objeto).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct SymbolicFact {
    pub id: String,
    pub subject: Atom,
    pub relation: RelationType,
    pub object: Atom,
    pub strength: f32,       // Força da relação (0.0 - 1.0)
    pub confidence: f32,     // Confiança na relação (0.0 - 1.0)
    pub provenance: Option<String>,
    pub metadata: HashMap<String, serde_json::Value>,
    pub created_at: chrono::DateTime<chrono::Utc>,
}

impl SymbolicFact {
    pub fn new(subject: Atom, relation: RelationType, object: Atom) -> Self {
        Self {
            id: uuid::Uuid::new_v4().to_string(),
            subject,
            relation,
            object,
            strength: 1.0,
            confidence: 1.0,
            provenance: None,
            metadata: HashMap::new(),
            created_at: chrono::Utc::now(),
        }
    }

    pub fn with_strength(mut self, strength: f32) -> Self {
        self.strength = strength.clamp(0.0, 1.0);
        self
    }

    pub fn with_confidence(mut self, confidence: f32) -> Self {
        self.confidence = confidence.clamp(0.0, 1.0);
        self
    }

    pub fn with_provenance(mut self, provenance: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        self.provenance = Some(provenance.into());
        self
    }

    pub fn to_triple(&self) -> (Term, RelationType, Term) {
        (self.subject.term.clone(), self.relation.clone(), self.object.term.clone())
    }

    /// Converte para uma relação.
    pub fn to_relation(&self) -> Relation {
        Relation {
            id: self.id.clone(),
            relation_type: self.relation.clone(),
            subject: self.subject.clone(),
            object: self.object.clone(),
            strength: self.strength,
            confidence: self.confidence,
            provenance: self.provenance.clone(),
            created_at: self.created_at,
        }
    }
}

impl From<Relation> for SymbolicFact {
    fn from(rel: Relation) -> Self {
        Self {
            id: rel.id,
            subject: rel.subject,
            relation: rel.relation_type,
            object: rel.object,
            strength: rel.strength,
            confidence: rel.confidence,
            provenance: rel.provenance,
            metadata: HashMap::new(),
            created_at: rel.created_at,
        }
    }
}
```
